correctness.rationale: For finite connected complete multipartite graphs, geodesic 3-vertex sets at d>=2 are exactly part multiplicity 2+1; diameter <=2 makes this independent of d. Three-uniform clique maximum is 2 if no part has >=2, 3 if exactly one part has >=2, and 4 if at least two do. Monochromatic 2+1 avoidance gives chi=1 in the trivial all-singleton/edgeless cases; in two parts or with <=one nonsingleton part or max part<=2, explicit two-colorings work. K_(3,2,1) cannot use two colors because a pair must repeat in the three-part and forces a 2+1 triple in the remaining color; its omega is 4. Hereditary closure and the part-profile embedding show that any r>=3 with max>=3 and >=2 nonsingleton parts contains K_(3,2,1), and every smaller deletion avoids it. Independently enumerated 36 complete multipartite profiles through seven vertices and all induced profiles, corroborating the proof.
residual_risks: Scope is connected multipartite r>=3, k=3, d>=2; finite checker is not infinite proof.

originality.rationale: The exact result follows directly from two already published exact formulas: Chandran et al. (2025) Theorem 5.1 gives chi_gp for EVERY complete multipartite part-size profile; by the 2+1 geodesic identity this equals chi_d^3 for d>=2. Published Oct 4 SCOPE clique theorem gives omega_d^3=2+min(2,s), s=#n_i>=2. Their inequalities imply chi=ceil(omega/2) for every induced multipartite subgraph iff max part<=2 or s<=1 (or <=2 parts). The unique forbidden K_(3,2,1) is the elementary minimal failing part profile. New perfection vocabulary and the number-independent-of-d statement do not create mathematical novelty from this known combined implication.

Computer tests check small cases only; general proof stands independently as a corollary.
